admitted.text: She seems to survive by hiding behind a polished surface, and to have decided on the first night never to let Pace see past it again.
admitted.detail_quote: The one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: Randi reads as using polish and sexual command to cover raw needs for reassurance, possession, and a keepsake of her own.
admitted.detail_quote: Nothing ever happened to her. That was what the face was for.

admitted.text: What began as a game she planned seems to have become real desire for Vee, which surprises her.
admitted.detail_quote: I didn't think I'd like her this much. I keep waiting to get bored of her — I get bored of everybody — and it doesn't come.

admitted.text: She seems to tell herself that wanting Vee is only a task she does for Pace's plan.
admitted.detail_quote: For us, she said, after a second. When she's ready.

admitted.text: Randi reads as jealous of Pace’s access to Vee’s body, weekends, sleep, and private tenderness.
admitted.detail_quote: She had the rim of her glass in under her thumbnail, pressing, and she held it there until she set the glass down.

admitted.text: She reads as a skilled confidante who pulls Vee's secrets out of her and hands them back as gifts, both caring and manipulative.
admitted.detail_quote: I know exactly what I'm doing. I have always known what I'm doing.

admitted.text: Randi seems to use warmth as both genuine affection and a practiced instrument for directing people without their noticing the direction.
admitted.detail_quote: Randi listened the way she listened, which was completely

admitted.text: Finding her own name on the fraudulent loans reads as a wound to her pride in her family that she can't speak about.
admitted.detail_quote: The color had gone out of it. Her jaw had set.

admitted.text: He reads as truly careful about consent, and he holds to it even against Randi's impatience.
admitted.detail_quote: She chooses it, Randi. Every step of it. Or it isn't anything.

admitted.text: Pace reads as exceptionally attentive, making care tangible through food, warmth, craft, patience, and exact observation.
admitted.detail_quote: He hadn't told her it didn't matter. He'd gone and made her a place instead.

admitted.text: He seems generous with everything except words, and he answers Vee's veiled declaration of love by sidestepping it.
admitted.detail_quote: I love how good we are together.

admitted.text: He reads as someone who expresses affection and devotion through material care and service rather than verbal declarations.
admitted.detail_quote: He hadn't told her it didn't matter. He'd gone and made her a place instead.

admitted.text: For all his close attention to bodies, he seems blind to Randi's emotional pain.
admitted.detail_quote: He set each piece beside the next and they would not go together into anything he could name

admitted.text: He seems too quick to accept the easy explanation Randi offers when she cries.
admitted.detail_quote: it was the want, he thought, with an edge on it tonight

admitted.text: A cut-off from his family reads as an old wound he keeps tightly closed.
admitted.detail_quote: He had handed her the thing that had hurt him and named it luck.

admitted.text: He defends his teenage relationship with Daphne, and that reads as a harm he still calls luck.
admitted.detail_quote: He had handed her the thing that had hurt him and named it luck.

admitted.text: Pace also reads as dangerously confident that local consent is enough, despite Vee’s ignorance of the larger arrangement governing her choices.
admitted.detail_quote: She consents — every time — or I'm done.

admitted.text: She seems to carry her mother's shame inside her, so it judges her own desire as it happens.
admitted.detail_quote: the word arriving whole and in her mother's voice before she had finished forming the picture

admitted.text: She reads as starved in a way that goes far deeper than food.
admitted.detail_quote: Even when I was hungry, it was never quite the thing I wanted. I didn't know food could be the thing you wanted. Then you cooked for me.

admitted.text: She seems drawn to Randi in a way she won't let herself name.
admitted.detail_quote: And then Randi's mouth, easy, only what they did — except that this time, when it should have ended, Vee was the one who wouldn't let it

admitted.text: She seems to trust Randi completely, even reverently, and has no idea she was chosen on purpose.
admitted.detail_quote: It had come to her all of a piece, the one and then the other, in six weeks, for no reason she had done anything to deserve.

admitted.text: She reads as quietly loyal, protecting Randi's shame without being asked.
admitted.detail_quote: She didn't look back at the point, and she didn't say the name, and she didn't tell Randi, then or after, what she'd seen.

admitted.text: By the end she seems worn down by a love that has no name.
admitted.detail_quote: She had no name for the best thing in her life, not the big one he wouldn't give her and not the small one she couldn't find

admitted.text: She reads as a fiercely protective friend who acts instead of talking.
admitted.detail_quote: The whole forty seconds Vee had spent being a student, Cassie had spent watching what the dress had done to her friend

admitted.text: Cassie reads as Vee’s most reliable friend because she sees closely without demanding performance or enlarging pain for her own gratification.
admitted.detail_quote: Cassie never asked — asking was for people who wanted the sad version to get bigger.

admitted.text: She seems to sense something wrong about Randi early, without being able to say what.
admitted.detail_quote: She didn't take the bit's open door — didn't do the *oh, mine's a whole thing too* that the bit was built to be answered with

admitted.text: She reads as a gracious house president who quietly keeps track of Randi's secrets.
admitted.detail_quote: Brooke was the chapter president and did not need to stand to stop someone in her own common room.

admitted.text: She seems to be Pace's blunt, clear-eyed friend, who sees the cost of the arrangement coming.
admitted.detail_quote: If that's not already complicated, it will be. But I bet it's worth it.

admitted.text: She reads as harmless comic chorus, a friend to Vee without agenda — one of the few
admitted.detail_quote: We're doing hair Saturday. I'm coming to your room.

admitted.text: the bench beneath the table: hidden appetite and control disguised as ordinary domestic furniture
admitted.detail_quote: full of what it was, doing what it would continue to do, waiting for the next time.

admitted.text: The deadbolt Randi always turns: her habit of locking her inner self away.
admitted.detail_quote: the size of a key turning in a lock.

admitted.text: Thin-sliced apples: feeding as how love works in this book, and appetite as a way of letting go.
admitted.detail_quote: a girl who had been portioning herself, weighing every want before she let herself have it

admitted.text: The burgundy silk: being seen as she actually is, rather than as she imagined herself.
admitted.detail_quote: Everything she'd ever worn had been cut for no one in particular. This one had been cut to the actual shape of her, and to no one else's.

admitted.text: The flannel shirt: Pace's presence, which fades without him and has to be refilled.
admitted.detail_quote: the heat in the shirt was her own, given back. He wasn't in it.

admitted.text: Vee's green panties: a token of Vee that Pace keeps and Randi has never been offered.
admitted.detail_quote: Her hand with the green in it stayed flat against his chest, and he could feel the satin there between her palm and his skin

admitted.text: the top bathroom drawer: Pace’s acts creating space for Vee before his words define her place
admitted.detail_quote: He'd folded his whole ordered self down into a single drawer. He'd given her the top one.

admitted.text: Simpson's paradox: the same facts tell opposite stories depending on how the three of them are grouped.
admitted.detail_quote: Each year on its own, the first man is the better hitter. Put the two years together and the second man is.

admitted.text: The outlier that carries forward: a hidden departure that taints everything after it.
admitted.detail_quote: It's in everything that comes after.

admitted.text: Randi’s untouched small bowl: the portion Pace assigns her and the tenderness she cannot receive while feeling displaced by Vee
admitted.detail_quote: the one line she had drawn through it still there

admitted.text: Vee lying bare in the cold: the failure of substitutes and her refusal, for one night, to let borrowed warmth cover the central absence
admitted.detail_quote: She lay there with nothing on her in the cold

admitted.text: Will Vee find out that Randi and Pace are lovers who chose her together?
admitted.detail_quote: She is the first woman Randi has ever let herself want.

admitted.text: Will Pace ever give Vee the word, or a name for what they are?
admitted.detail_quote: She had said her best sentence. He had not said the sentence back.

admitted.text: What is the story behind the scar on Pace's thigh?
admitted.detail_quote: He kept it there under his, on the thing he wasn't going to tell her about yet

admitted.text: What happened between Pace and his mother?
admitted.detail_quote: He had taken his mother out of the answer.

admitted.text: What happened when Pace forced his way past Daphne's "door"?
admitted.detail_quote: Daphne had built a door, once, and he had not respected it.

admitted.text: Will Vee learn that Randi's "European" accent is really hidden Kentucky?
admitted.detail_quote: more of whatever it was than there had been

admitted.text: What will Randi do about her father's fraud, and will she ever learn that Vee saw?
admitted.detail_quote: Randi had no idea she'd been looked at.

admitted.text: After a weekend away and a sleepless night, will Vee go back to Pace unchanged after the break?
admitted.detail_quote: She had everything he did and not the one thing he wouldn't say, and there was no name in her for it
